sections.html:
Brookings is the county seat of Brookings County, about 60 miles north of Sioux Falls on Interstate 29. The 2020 census counted 23,377 residents. South Dakota State University enrolled 12,065 students in fall 2024 and is the city's largest employer, so the housing market follows the academic calendar.

Duplexes, older single-family homes near campus and student rentals sit next to family neighborhoods on the edge of town. Owners who inherited a rental, or who rented to students for years, often end up selling a house with worn finishes and a tenant lease that runs to a fixed date. Timing a sale around the spring and summer lease cycle can matter more here than in a town without a campus. Unemployment was 2.5 percent in December 2024, and a tight job market tends to keep buyer demand steady. It will not rescue a house that needs heavy work.

Brookings runs rental inspections and licensing through its Code Enforcement office. A rental dwelling is inspected and carries a license for up to four years, or as an ordinance requires, and each unit has a maximum occupant count.

  • The form is the Rental Housing Permit Application.
  • Tenants with occupancy concerns can use the city's complaint form.
  • For fees, call Code Enforcement at (605) 692-6629.

If you are selling a rental, find out when the license expires and what occupant limit applies. A buyer who plans to keep the tenants will ask. A lapsed license or an old inspection finding is easier to fix before a contract is signed than after.

Read the lease too. A fixed end date, a deposit you must transfer, or a tenant who will not allow showings all change how and when the house can sell.

Brookings County bills in two halves. Notices go out in January, and you can pay the whole year once you have the notice.

PaymentDue dateNotes
First halfApril 30Mailed payments must be postmarked by this date
Second halfOctober 31Same postmark rule
Special assessmentsApril 30Due in full
Any bill under $50April 30Due in full

sections.h2: Paying the bill and tax relief
sections.html:
The Auditor and Treasurer share one office at 520 3rd Street, Suite 100, Brookings, SD 57006. You can pay at the counter, by mail, online, or through the drop box on the west side of the building. Credit cards carry a 2.5 percent service fee at the counter. Partial payments are not accepted on taxes that are due or delinquent.

Two relief programs are offered there: the Disabled Veteran and Surviving Spouse exemption, and the Senior Citizens and Disabled assessment freeze. If you qualify, ask the office how a sale affects the benefit before you list.

On a sale, the unpaid share of the current year's bill is normally settled through the title company at closing. Ask for a payoff figure early so no surprise shows up on the settlement statement.

sections.h2: Is flood risk a factor for Brookings sellers?
sections.html:
It can be for houses near creeks. The city's Engineering Division keeps pages on floodplains and on Six-Mile Creek flood risk mitigation, and the future land use map overlays the Six Mile Creek and Deer Creek floodplains.

FEMA publishes the floodplain boundary. Look up your parcel on FEMA's map or ask city engineering staff whether the house is inside it. A buyer will likely ask, and the seller's disclosure form has a question about flood plains, so the answer has to be written down either way.

sections.h2: Winter wear on a Brookings house
sections.html:
Brookings has long, cold winters. About 35 days a year bring lows below zero, and snowfall runs about 35.8 inches. Cold snaps stress furnaces, water heaters and older plumbing, and spring melt tests sump pumps and basement walls.

Buyers' inspectors here routinely look at furnace age, window condition and signs of water in the lower level. A seller who already knows the answers before the inspection is in a better spot to negotiate. Have the furnace serviced and clear out the basement so the walls can be seen.

South Dakota law requires the seller to give the buyer a property condition disclosure. The state form, dated 07/2025, asks about liens, easements, drainage, the roof, radon, lead paint, mold and the working status of about 47 systems and appliances.

The deed needs a Certificate of Real Estate Value (PT 56) before the register of deeds will record it. The transfer fee comes from SDCL 43-4-21, and SDCL 43-4-22 lists 19 exemptions. Minnehaha County charges $1.00 per thousand, which gives a sense of the scale. Call the Brookings County Register of Deeds for its recording fee and the amount due on your sale.

sections.h2: When does a cash sale make sense in Brookings?
sections.html:
A cash sale suits an owner who needs speed or does not want to repair and show a house. Inherited homes, worn student rentals and houses with deferred maintenance are the usual cases.

We buy Brookings houses as-is, with no repairs required, and you owe nothing if you decline the offer. A cash sale skips the listing photos, the open houses, the buyer's loan approval and the repair requests that follow an inspection. You pick the closing date. Before you accept, gather your latest tax bill, any rental license and lease papers, and the disclosure form, so the title company has what it needs.

If the house is a rental with tenants in place, tell us the lease end date up front. That detail shapes the offer and the closing timeline more than almost anything else.

faqs.q: How many people live in Brookings, SD?
faqs.a: The 2020 census counted 23,377 residents, and the Census Bureau estimates 25,355 as of July 1, 2025.

faqs.q: Do Brookings rental houses need a license?
faqs.a: Yes. Code Enforcement inspects rental dwellings and issues licenses for up to four years, with a maximum occupant count for each unit.

faqs.q: When are property taxes due in Brookings County?
faqs.a: The first half is due April 30 and the second half October 31. Special assessments and any bill under $50 are due in full by April 30.

faqs.q: Can I pay Brookings County taxes online?
faqs.a: Yes. Online payment by card, PayPal or e-check is available, along with in-person, mail and drop-box payments. Cards at the counter carry a 2.5 percent fee.

faqs.q: Does a Brookings seller have to complete a disclosure form, and what is the PT 56?
faqs.a: Yes, South Dakota requires the seller's property condition disclosure. The PT 56 is the Certificate of Real Estate Value, which lists buyer, seller, legal description, price and terms, and the register of deeds cannot record a deed without it.
